Subjective - The patient twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb this morning and now walks with a limp. Swelling appeared within an hour. No numbness in the toes.
Objective - Vitals: pulse 88, respirations 18, blood pressure 126/82, temperature 36.9 C, oxygen saturation 99 percent on room air. Right ankle shows swelling over the lateral malleolus with tenderness; the skin is intact; the toes move freely.
Assessment - Lateral ankle sprain, right.
Plan - Apply ice for twenty minutes several times per day and elevate above heart level when seated. Use an elastic wrap for compression and avoid weight-bearing exercise this week. Follow up if swelling worsens or weight bearing remains impossible after five days.
